feat userver/proto-structs: tests and fixes

* Stabilize the serialization API for Well-known types
* Introduce an extendable discovery system for Well-known types
   * Suppose that a proto struct uses `foo::bar::Something` for a field type, which is NOT a Protobuf type
   * Then `<userver/proto-structs/io/foo/bar/something.hpp>` should bring in the type definition (usually by including the proper header)
   * Then `<userver/proto-structs/io/foo/bar/something_conv.hpp>` should bring in proto-structs serialization for the type
   * Serialization discovery was inspired by userver chaotic and postgres
* Implement serialization for all main Well-known types: integers, strings, optional, vector, maps, `utils::Box`,
* Implement the collection of path to the current Protobuf node in case of a convertion error
* Add diverse conversion tests for various hand-written proto structs

* Make topological sort stable for build stability and nicer output
* Only forward declare types when actually needed
* Clean up produced whitespace, generated code is now almost perfectly formatted
* Clean up exception messages

or [DeleteObject](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/API/API_DeleteObject.html#API_DeleteObject_ResponseSyntax). In this pr I have removed `OK` text from body for 200 responses.

List of affected methods:

1. PutObject
2. DeleteObject
3. CopyObject
4. HeadObject

feat core: add "core" http client without plugins

Basic HTTP client settings are moved to the new component `http-client-core`. This means a breaking change going from userver 2.13 to userver 2.14.

Migration guide:

1. For each @ref components::HttpClient you add to components list manually you should also add corresponding @ref components::HttpClientCore
   For example:

   ```cpp
   #include <userver/clients/http/component.hpp>

   components::ComponentList MyComponentList() {
       return components::ComponentList()
           ...
           .Append<components::HttpClientCore>("my-http-client-core")
           .Append<components::HttpClient>("my-http-client")
           ...;
   }
   ```

   Core counterparts of common HttpClients are already appended to @ref components::CommonComponentList()

2. In your `static_config.yaml` all @ref components::HttpClient settings should be moved to corresponding core component settings except for plugins.
   You should also add `core-component: <name of corresponding HttpClientCore component>` to each HttpClient settings.
   For example:

   ```yaml
   http-client:
       core-component: http-client-core  # default value, may be omitted
       plugins:
           my-plugin-name: 1
   http-client-core:
       fs-task-processor: $fs-task-processor
       user-agent: $user-agent

   # In case you also have "http-client-statistics" component:
   http-client-statistics:
       core-component: http-client-statistics-core
   http-client-statistics-core:
       user-agent: $user-agent
       fs-task-processor: $fs-task-processor
       thread-name-prefix: stats
   ```

fix grpc: trim whitespaces in status message

The gRPC specification requires status-messages to be percent-encoded
but allows spaces (0x20) to remain unencoded. However, this conflicts
with HTTP/2 RFC9113 which strictly forbids leading and trailing
whitespace in header field values. This fix trims whitespaces from gRPC
status messages before transmission to ensure compliance with HTTP/2

feat core: use separate http client plugins list for dynamic configs

Several changes are made in order to support dynamic config subscription in http client plugins:

1. Plugins are renamed to middlewares
2. Middlewares static configuration for @ref clients::HttpClient is updated to be more like @ref scripts/docs/en/userver/grpc/client\_middlewares.md
3. @ref clients::http::MiddlewarePipelineComponent are introduced to manage common middlewares settings
4. Dynamic configs use separate @ref clients::HttpClient instance named `dynamic-config-http-client`, so that middlewares that use dynamic configs may be disabled just for dynamic configs client and enabled for all other clients in `http-client-middleware-pipeline.middlewares`

Migration guide:

1. Make sure that you use `.AppendComponentList(clients::http::ComponentList())` in your component list instead of `.Append<components::HttpClientCore>().Append<components::HttpClient>()`
2. For classes inherited from @ref tracing::TracingManagerBase:
   1. Change @ref clients::http::PluginRequest in @ref tracing::TracingManagerBase::FillRequestWithTracingContext() parameters to @ref clients::http::MiddlewareRequest
3. For classes inherited from @ref clients::http::Plugin:
   1. Replace `#include <userver/clients/http/plugin.hpp>` with `#include <userver/clients/http/middlewares/base.hpp>`
   2. Change base class to @ref clients::http::MiddlewareBase
   3. Change @ref clients::http::PluginRequest in methods parameters to @ref clients::http::MiddlewareRequest
   4. Stop passing middleware name to  base class constructor
   5. Empty methods implementations (or `return true;` for @ref clients::http::MiddlewareBase::HookOnRetry()) may be omitted

   For example:

   ```diff
   -#include <userver/clients/http/plugin.hpp>
   +#include <userver/clients/http/middlewares/base.hpp>
   ...

   -class MyPlugin : public clients::http::Plugin {
   +class MyMiddleware : public clients::http::MiddlewareBase {
   public:
   ...
   -    MyPlugin() : clients::http::Plugin("my-plugin") {}
   +    MyMiddleware() : clients::http::MiddlewareBase() {}

   -    void HookPerformRequest(clients::http::PluginRequest& request) override { do_something(request); }
   +    void HookPerformRequest(clients::http::MiddlewareRequest& request) override { do_something(request); };

   -    void HookCreateSpan(clients::http::PluginRequest&, tracing::Span&) override {}
   -    void HookOnCompleted(clients::http::PluginRequest&, clients::http::Response&) override {}
   -    void HookOnError(clients::http::PluginRequest&, std::error_code) override {}
   -    bool HookOnRetry(clients::http::PluginRequest&) override { return true; }

   };
   ```
4. For plugin components inherited from @ref clients::http::plugin::ComponentBase:
   1. Replace `#include <userver/clients/http/plugin_component.hpp>` with `#include <userver/clients/http/middlewares/component.hpp>`
   2. Change base class to @ref clients::http::middlewares::ComponentBase
   3. Component name is not required to have prefix `http-client-plugin-` anymore, `http-client-` prefix is suggested instead
   4. Rename `GetPlugin` method to `GetMiddleware`, change its return type to `clients::http::MiddlewareBase`
   5. Use @ref dynamic\_config::Source::UpdateAndListen() to subscribe on dynamic config updates
   6. Pass middleware index to base class constructor, instead of setting it in config file

   For example:

   ```diff
   -#include <userver/clients/http/plugin_component.hpp>
   +#include <userver/clients/http/middlewares/component.hpp>
   ...

   -class SomeComponentName : public clients::http::plugin::ComponentBase {
   +class SomeComponentName : public clients::http::middlewares::ComponentBase {
   public:
   -    static constexpr std::string_view kName = "http-client-plugin-my-plugin-name";
   +    static constexpr std::string_view kName = "http-client-my-middleware-name";

   -    SomeComponentName(const components::ComponentConfig& config, const components::ComponentContext& context)
   -        : ComponentBase(config, context),
   -          plugin_(std::make_unique<Plugin>()),
   +    SomeComponentName(const components::ComponentConfig& config, const components::ComponentContext& context)
   +        : ComponentBase(config, context, clients::http::middlewares::MiddlewareIndex{1234}),
   +          middleware_(std::make_unique<Middleware>()),
   {
       auto& config_component = context.FindComponent<components::DynamicConfig>();
       subscriber_scope_ =
   -        components::DynamicConfig::NoblockSubscriber{config_component}
   -            .GetEventSource()
   -            .AddListener(this, kName, &Component::OnConfigUpdate);
   +        config_component
   +            .GetSource()
   +            .UpdateAndListen(this, kName, &Component::OnConfigUpdate);
   }
   ...
   -    clients::http::Plugin& GetPlugin() override { return *plugin_; }
   +    clients::http::MiddlewareBase& GetMiddleware() override { return *middleware_; }

   private:
   -    std::unique_ptr<clients::http::Plugin> plugin_;
   +    std::unique_ptr<clients::http::MiddlewareBase> middleware_;
   };
   ```
5. Make the following changes in static config:
   1. In every @ref components::HttpClient config, rename `plugins` to `middlewares`
   2. Update middleware component names to current `Component::kName`
   3. Use full middleware components names as keys and `{enabled: true}` as values in `middlewares` for every @ref components::HttpClient config
   4. Move middlewares that you want to use for all @ref components::HttpClient instances from `http-client.middlewares` to `http-client-middleware-pipeline.middlewares`
   5. Set `dynamic-config-http-client.middlewares.<middleware name>.enabled` to `false` for all middlewares that are subscribed to dynamic configs updates

   For example:

   ```diff
   components_manager:
       components:
   -        http-client-plugin-common-plugin-name:
   +        http-client-common-middleware-name:
               ...
   -        http-client-plugin-plugin-with-dynamic-config:
   +        http-client-middleware-with-dynamic-config:
               ...

   -    http-client:
   -        plugins:
   -            common-plugin-name: 1
   -            with-dynamic-config: 2
   +    http-client-middleware-pipeline:
   +        middlewares:
   +            http-client-common-middleware-name:
   +                enabled: true
   +            http-client-middleware-with-dynamic-config:
   +                enabled: true
   +    dynamic-config-http-client:
   +        middlewares:
   +            http-client-middleware-with-dynamic-config:
   +                enabled: false
   ```

It is very useful in testing env where mysql database is running inside of docker container and there is no need to worry about SSL.

P.S. sample service was working fine because mysql database was running on localhost and in this case libmariadb using a unix socket and no SSL needed at all.

fix postgresql: optimize distlock locking

The original request took a lock on the row even if this distlock had already been captured by another owner. However, the transaction did not make any changes. As a result, all attempts to take a lock for one key were lined up.

Now, instead of unconditional locking, we get an analog of double check locking at the request level.

This change adds a check that there are no current distlock from another owner before executing the INSERT.

If SELECT finds the current distlock, then there will be no lock. Moreover: the transaction itself will not become writing (you can check it via `SELECT txid_current_if_assigned()`).

refactor engine: avoid AfterWait() in FdPoller

* Add `WaitListLightWithEpoch` that ignores the notification if the epoch passed with the notification does not match the epoch set by the `Awaiter`
   * An epoch separate from `Awaiter`'s `context` is required, because:
      1. A single epoch is set per multiple wait operations, so the previous notification may be OK for a while (e.g. for multiple waits of `GetAll`), but it can be explicitly cut off by the awaiter side
      2. `context` is not an epoch, it can have arbitrary meaning, e.g. it can always have the same value for each iteration
* Add an optional epoch to `ev::Watcher`. The callback can get the epoch value with which the `Watcher` was started
* Use them in `FdPoller`. Only wake up the task if the epoch of the `Awaitable` is the same as the epoch with which the `Watcher` was started. This avoids spurious wakeups without the need for synchronous `Stop`


Benchmark results analysis:

* `RcuMapConcurrentInsert` is O(N\^2). Filling a map of 10000 elements takes multiple seconds (locally), so this one benchmark instantiation was not included in the PR.
  * `MonotonicSetConcurrentInsert` is a reasonable O(N).
* Lookups are blazing-fast with `MonotonicConcurrentSet`. As little as 1 nanosecond is added to `Hash` and `KeyEqual` overhead, with no contention whatsoever.
* Concurrent insertions are also very fast with `MonotonicConcurrentSet`, with reasonably low contention overhead. Due to the bucket-locked mutation implementation, threads sometimes have to sleep while another thread emplaces an item into the same bucket.

Further future optimizations are possible:

* An empty `MonotonicConcurrentSet` could be made to have no table, drastically reducing memory overhead. libc\+\+ also does this optimization. This helps in usages where most containers are empty.
* Time spent under global lock in `Grow` could be minimized. One possible strategy is to keep two tables at the same time (current and next) and insert items to both tables. When the time comes, just allocate a new next table and declare the old next table as current.

feat userver: handle non-101 HTTP responses in WebSocket handshake

#### Summary

Fixed WebSocket client to properly handle HTTP error responses (401, 403, etc.) during handshake instead of treating them as connection errors.

#### Problem

curl expects 101 status for WebSocket upgrade. When server returns other HTTP status (e.g., 401 Unauthorized), curl reports `kHttpReturnedError`, preventing client code from accessing the actual HTTP response.

#### Solution

Ignore curl error in `request_state.cpp` for WebSocket handshake when a valid HTTP status code is received. This allows client to inspect response status, headers, and body.

feat ydb: switch `Transaction` and `ExecuteDataQuery` from Table Client to Query Client API

## Replace Table Service with Query Service for YDB Transactions

### 📝 Summary of Changes:

#### 1. Transaction Class Header (`transaction.hpp`)

- **Line 5**: Changed include to `<ydb-cpp-sdk/client/query/query.h>` for transaction types
- **Line 74**: Changed constructor parameter from `NYdb::NTable::TTransaction` to `NYdb::NQuery::TTransaction`
- **Line 90**: Changed member variable from `NYdb::NTable::TTransaction ydb_tx_` to `NYdb::NQuery::TTransaction ydb_tx_`

#### 2. Transaction Implementation (`transaction.cpp`)

- **Constructor (Lines 22-37)**: Updated to accept `NYdb::NQuery::TTransaction` instead of Table transaction
- **Commit() (Lines 70-101)**: Uses `ydb_tx_.Commit()` with Query Client settings
- **Rollback() (Lines 103-122)**: Uses `ydb_tx_.Rollback()` with Query Client settings
- **Execute() (Lines 138-176)**: Uses `ydb_tx_.GetSession().ExecuteQuery()` with Query Client APIs and `impl::ConvertStatsMode()`
- **GetBuilder() (Lines 124-126)**: Uses `ydb_tx_.GetSession().GetParamsBuilder()`

#### 3. TableClient Implementation (`table.cpp`)

- **Begin() (Lines 297-314)**: Changed from Table Client to Query Client (RetryQuery, PrepareQueryTxSettings, BeginTransaction)
- **ExecuteDataQuery() (Lines 352-384)**: Migrated to use Query Client:
  - Uses `RetryQuery` instead of `RetryOperation`
  - Converts `QuerySettings` to `NYdb::NQuery::TExecuteQuerySettings` using `impl::ConvertStatsMode()`
  - Uses `PrepareQueryTxSettings` instead of `PrepareTxSettings`
  - Uses `NYdb::NQuery::TSession`, `TTxControl`, and `ExecuteQuery`

#### 4. Implementation Utilities (`impl/operation_settings.hpp`, `impl/operation_settings.cpp`)

- **ConvertStatsMode()**: Single shared implementation that converts `NYdb::NTable::ECollectQueryStatsMode` to `NYdb::NQuery::EStatsMode`
- Eliminates code duplication between transaction.cpp and table.cpp

#### 5. Build Configuration (`CMakeLists.txt`, Line 8)

- Added `YDB-CPP-SDK::Query` to YDB\_LIBRARIES list

### 🔑 Key Technical Decisions:

1. **Complete Migration**: Both `Transaction::Execute()` and `TableClient::ExecuteDataQuery()` now use Query Client
2. **No Code Duplication**: Consolidated `ConvertStatsMode()` into shared impl namespace
3. **Transaction Object Model**: Query Client provides `NYdb::NQuery::TTransaction` with similar pattern to Table Client
4. **API Conversion**: Consistent pattern for converting QuerySettings across both implementations
5. **Backward Compatibility**: All public APIs remain unchanged - only internal implementation uses Query Client

### 🎯 Benefits:

- Uses modern Query Client API throughout instead of deprecated Table Client
- Maintains full backward compatibility with existing code
- Follows YDB SDK recommended migration path
- No code duplication - single ConvertStatsMode implementation
- Consistent implementation pattern across Transaction and TableClient
- No changes required to existing code using these APIs

### 📚 References:

- Issue: userver-framework/userver#1061
- YDB Go SDK example: <https://github.com/ydb-platform/ydb-go-sdk/blob/70fd60ba1490c984162574958dd23344cb513f6e/internal/table/session.go#L131-L165>
- YDB Java SDK example: <https://github.com/ydb-platform/ydb-java-sdk/blob/3fd06ddcf36ab918eb6a394ee3bbebac6caf15b2/query/src/main/java/tech/ydb/query/impl/TableClientImpl.java#L106-L160>

fix upg: use CriticalAsyncBackground to clean up connections so the cleanup task doesn’t inherit the original task’s deadline

Previously, connection cleanup in `upg` used `CriticalAsync`. By design, `CriticalAsync` inherits the parent context (including its deadline/cancellation).

When an HTTP/GRPC handler timed out or was cancelled, the inherited context would cancel the cleanup task as well. As a result, connections created within the handler often didn’t have a chance to be cleaned up properly.

Connection cleanup now runs via `CriticalAsyncBackground`, which executes the cleanup task in a background context. The cleanup task no longer inherits the parent handler’s deadline/cancellation.

feat s3api: Add URL encoding for S3 object keys

# S3 URL Encoding Fix

## Problem
S3 API methods (`GetObject`, `PutObject`, etc.) failed with object keys containing special characters (spaces, Cyrillic, etc.) because they weren't being URL-encoded.
`Bad URL, curl error: malformed input, url: https://mybucket.s3-some-site.awsornot.com/path/to/object with : spaces`

## Solution
Added two functions for proper S3 object key encoding, compatible with AWS SDK behavior:

- **`UrlEncodePathSegment()`** - encodes a single path segment, preserving RFC 3986 unreserved chars (`-`, `_`, `.`, `~`) and S3-safe chars (`$`, `&`, `,`, `:`, `=`, `@`)
- **`EncodeS3Key()`** - encodes S3 object key, preserving `/` as path separators

Implementation follows AWS SDK approach: [aws-sdk-cpp/URI.cpp](https://github.com/aws/aws-sdk-cpp/blob/master/aws-cpp-sdk-core/source/http/URI.cpp#L54-L60)

**Examples:**
```cpp
EncodeS3Key("folder/file with spaces.txt")  // → "folder/file%20with%20spaces.txt"
EncodeS3Key("folder/файл.txt")              // → "folder/%D1%84%D0%B0%D0%B9%D0%BB.txt"
```

## Changes
- **universal/http/url.hpp, url.cpp**: New encoding functions
- **universal/http/url_test.cpp**: new tests
- **libraries/s3api/s3api_methods.cpp**: Apply `EncodeS3Key()` to all S3 methods

`Producer::Send` пытается обработать ошибки переполнения локальной очереди librdkafka в пределах настроенного `delivery.timeout.ms`.

В отличие от старых методов `Send` и `SendAsync` метод порождает только одну корутину на всю пачку сообщений.

fix mongo: deadline propagation stale snapshot on connection creation

When a new MongoDB connection needs to be created (no idle connections in pool),
Create() runs a ping to MongoDB without any deadline enforcement — it is bounded
only by SOCKETTIMEOUTMS from the URI config (typically several seconds).

Meanwhile, MakeRequestContext() captures the remaining deadline as a snapshot
*before* calling GetClient(), so if Create() takes several seconds the snapshot
becomes stale. The stale value is then used as maxTimeMS for the actual query,
causing requests to run far beyond the original deadline.

Example: deadline=999ms, Create() takes ~6.9s ping, then query runs another
999ms → total 7.883s with "operation exceeded time limit" from MongoDB.

Fix in collection_impl.cpp: After GetClient() returns, re-evaluate the
remaining deadline with a fresh GetDeadlineTimeLeft() call. If the deadline has
already expired, throw CancelledException immediately. Pass the fresh value as
inherited_deadline so maxTimeMS is computed correctly.

crypto: add PublicKey::LoadFromPrivateKey and tests

This PR refers to [issue #665](https://github.com/userver-framework/userver/issues/665).

Added PublicKey::LoadFromPrivateKey(const PrivateKey&) to userver::crypto to derive a public key from an already loaded private key.

Implementation is minimal and additive: it validates input, uses OpenSSL to extract/load the public key, and throws crypto::KeyParseError on failures.

Test coverage added in universal/src/crypto/public_key_test.cpp:
1) RSA happy path (sign with private, verify with derived public)
2) EC happy path
3) empty PrivateKey{} -> KeyParseError

Test keys for this are reused from existing crypto tests to keep fixtures consistent: RSA key from universal/src/crypto/signature_test.cpp, EC key from universal/src/crypto/public_key_test.cpp.

Dropped clang-14 support, allowed using C++20 ranges in userver implementation.

feat ydb: add TopicWriteSession support

`TopicClient` had read session support but no write session support, requiring users to call `GetNativeTopicClient()` directly.

This PR adds `TopicWriteSession` -- a thin coroutine-friendly wrapper over `NYdb::NTopic::IWriteSession`, mirroring the existing `TopicReadSession` pattern:

- `GetEvent()` -- suspends the coroutine via `impl::GetFutureValue(WaitEvent())`, then returns the event
- `TryGetEvent()` -- non-blocking poll, returns `nullopt` if no event is buffered

bug userver/postgresql: handle BindComplete message from PG correctly in non-pipeline mode

TL;DR:
Our libpq fork handles the BindComplete message incorrectly. As a result, when Odyssey started sending it and ReadyForQuery in separate packets, the service started crashing (core dumping).

What is happening:
- During the portal bind, we send the >B/S messages.
- In response, Odyssey sends <2.
- When we read the bind result:
	- Due to a bug, we read the first packet containing 2.
	- While processing it, we change the connection state to IDLE.
	- We do not read (consume) the second packet containing Z.
- Next, during the portal execute, we send the >D/E/S messages.
- When we read the execute result:
	- We read the packet containing Z (leftover from the previous step).
	- While processing it, we transition the connection state to IDLE.
	- Because of this state, fetching the result returns a nullptr, causing the code to core dump.

Relates: https://nda.ya.ru/t/KJPGNoeg7c8qKD

cc core: stabilize flaky timeout metrics in tests-deadline

**Symptoms:** `test_timeout_expired` and `test_timeout_expired_with_reuse` sometimes failed on `httpclient.errors{http_error=timeout}` — expected N, got 0 or N−1.

feat server/http, ugrpc: graceful shutdown 2nd stage

Add a new (2nd) stage to the graceful shutdown procedure.

The new procedure consists of 2 stages:

1. \[Existed before\] Health checks are being failed. Requests processing continues as usual. Special response headers are added, if enabled.
2. \[New\] Listeners are closed. So, new connections are not accepted. Already running requests have time to complete.

Stage enablements and lengths are controlled by new `graceful_shutdown_continue_accepting_requests_interval` and `graceful_shutdown_pending_requests_completion_interval` parameters of the `components::ManagerControllerComponent`, respectively.

The previous `graceful_shutdown_interval` parameter has been deprecated and should be migrated to the new parameters. Currently, it serves as a fallback for new parameters when they are not specified. However, it will be completely removed in the future.

refactor grpc: parse and serialize server messages from grpc::ByteBuffer manually

Switch the server `CompletionQueue` path to receive and send raw `grpc::ByteBuffer` messages while keeping the public service API typed. Requests and responses are now parsed/serialized inside userver, around the existing responder and call processor flow. It lets congestion control reject a call before we spend CPU parsing the unary request payload.

We intentionally do not use the gRPC generic API because:
- It loses the registered-method fast path with an internal precomputed table of RPC names and routes calls through generic method-name dispatch.
- It loses the inline initial-payload optimization for unary-request RPCs, requiring an extra `Read` operation through the stream with extra thread switching.

fix websocket: avoid size_t overflow in frame length check

1. payload_len is read straight from the 64-bit extended length field, so a client fully controls it.
2. the check `payload_len + frame.payload->size() > max_payload_size` wraps in size_t when payload_len is near SIZE_MAX, so after a 1-byte fragmented frame a continuation frame with extended length 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF passes the limit, the payload is resized to the wrapped near-zero size, and RecvExactly then writes payload_len bytes past the buffer.

Bound payload_len against max_payload_size before adding, then compare the current size against the remaining budget. max-remote-payload defaults to 65536 and the frame reader runs server-side on every client message.

feat core: use unsigned char for ctype calls in request header parsers

Repro: send a request whose `Authorization: Digest ...` or `Cookie` header contains a byte >= 0x80 (for example `Digest \xC3username=...`).
Cause: `ParseAuthInfo` and the cookie `Strip` helper walk the header with a signed `char` and hand each byte to `std::isalnum`/`std::isspace`. A byte >= 0x80 becomes a negative `int`, and passing a negative value other than `EOF` to the ctype functions is undefined behavior; on libc builds whose classification table is not defined below zero this is an out-of-bounds read.
Fix: classify the bytes as `unsigned char`, the same convention already used in `universal/src/http/url.cpp`.

Both headers are parsed before authentication, so any client can reach the call. Added a regression test that feeds a high-bit byte through the digest parser.

fix universal: fix ForwardLike in C++23 to behave same as std::forwad_like

`utils::ForwardLike` used `return x;` for the non-const lvalue-like case.

This no longer matches `std::forward_like` in C++23. Since P2266R3 ("Simpler implicit move"), the C++23 return statement rules treat a move-eligible returned expression as an xvalue. In standard wording this is the return statement wording in `[stmt.return]`: if the returned expression is move-eligible, it is treated as an xvalue. `std::forward_like<T>` still has to preserve the reference category requested by `T&&`, so `ForwardLike<int&>(...)` must produce an lvalue reference.

The existing `forward_like_test.cpp` fails with gcc 15.2.0:

```text
/home/egoncharov/bcore/cmake-build-debug/_deps/userver-src/universal/src/utils/forward_like_test.cpp:55:27:   required from here
   55 |     TestsTwoForwards<int&>(char{});
      |     ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^~~~~~~~
/home/egoncharov/bcore/cmake-build-debug/_deps/userver-src/universal/src/utils/forward_like_test.cpp:36:24: error: static assertion failed
   36 |     static_assert(std::is_same_v<
      |                   ~~~~~^~~~~~~~~~
   37 |                   decltype(std::forward_like<T>(std::forward<U>(x))),
      |                   ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
   38 |                   decltype(utils::ForwardLike<T>(std::forward<U>(x)))>);
      |                   ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
/home/egoncharov/bcore/cmake-build-debug/_deps/userver-src/universal/src/utils/forward_like_test.cpp:36:24: note: 'std::is_same_v<char&, char&&>' evaluates to false
```

This change implements `ForwardLike` via explicit casts to the expected reference type instead of relying on `return x`, `std::move`, or `std::as_const`.

Here is minimal demonsration of difference between original ForwardLike and std::forward_like in C++23:
https://godbolt.org/z/s7WdxYaWe

The implementation now:

* propagates `const` from `T` to the returned reference type;
* uses `T&&` to decide whether the result should be an lvalue reference or an rvalue reference;
* avoids dependence on C++23 return statement implicit move rules;
* matches `std::forward_like` semantics.

Testing:

* Built a userver-based project with `CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD=23`.
* Built and ran `userver-universal-unittest`.
* Full `userver-universal-unittest` run: 1671/1672 tests passed. The only failure was `LogFilepath.UserverCroppedCorrectly`, which appears to be path-layout-sensitive when userver is built as a CPM dependency under `_deps/userver-src`.

fix universal: fix random generator initialization in C++23

`utils::impl::RandomImpl` initialized `std::mt19937` via `AsLvalue(impl::MakeSeedSeq())`.

This fails to compile in C++23, because returning the rvalue-reference parameter from `AsLvalue` is affected by the C++23 implicit move rules from P2266R3. As a result, the returned expression may no longer be treated as a non-const lvalue reference, while the seed-sequence constructor of the generator expects a non-const lvalue seed sequence.

The error is (gcc 15.2.0):

```text
error: cannot bind non-const lvalue reference of type ‘std::seed_seq&’ to an rvalue of type ‘std::seed_seq’
```

This change removes the `AsLvalue` helper and initializes the generator from a local `std::seed_seq` object instead. The local object stays alive for the duration of the generator construction, and no reference to a temporary is returned.

fix cookie: validate Path/Domain/SameSite to block header injection

1. The cookie name and value are validated on construction, but the Path, Domain and SameSite attributes are set through SetPath/SetDomain/SetSameSite with no validation.
2. AppendToString writes those attributes verbatim into the Set-Cookie header, so a CR/LF in one of them injects a response header (HTTP response splitting) and a ';' injects an extra cookie-av.
3. They are reachable server side through HttpResponse::SetCookie and on the client side through Cookie::FromString when parsing an upstream Set-Cookie.
4. Reject control characters and ';' in those three setters via a shared ValidateCookieAttribute, matching the existing name/value checks, plus a regression test.

Repro before the patch: a cookie with SetPath("/\r\nSet-Cookie: admin=true") serializes to a Set-Cookie line carrying the raw CRLF, which splits the response.

fix testsuite: fix sql coverage with pytest 9.1.0+ (cmake build)

Changelog entry:

* Reworked injection of generated tests: SQL coverage and the service-runner
  default test are now produced through a single `pytest_generate_virtual_tests`
  hook provided by the new `pytest_userver.plugins.generated_tests` plugin.
  This fixes an issue where functional tests of services with postgresql and
  SQL coverage started to break down with `pytest >= 9.1.0`.

After updating to pytest 9.1.0 we observed the following issue: services
with generated SQL coverage testsuite tests started to break and hang when
trying to launch `start-*` cmake target. An inspection of test logs showed signs
that the root `conftest.py`, which may contain fixtures and mocks necessary
for service start, is ignored when in `start-*` mode.

A summary of the failure reason is that modern pytest is essentially more correct
in following is documented policies, while userver performed brittle tricks
with supplying custom generated tests.

Before test collection starts, pytest searches `conftest.py` files, which are
considered full-fledged plugins:
[initial conftests](https://docs.pytest.org/en/stable/how-to/writing_plugins.html#plugin-discovery-order-at-tool-startup).
These are `conftest.py` files which lie at the level of "root tests directory"
(which is determinted using an undocumented algorithm based on cwd and command
line args) or higher towards the filesystem root. Only those `conftest.py`,
for example, have a right to declare `pytest_plugins = ...`.

Now, as a part of "generated tests", we are also palming off an outside test
directory (built into userver) to pytest. This drives pytest crazy, and it chooses
a distant common parent as the root directory of tests. Because of this,
the `conftest.py` in the tests directory stops being considered the initial conftest,
and everything breaks down.

To fix this issue, instead of a physical test file, we now insert a virtual test
`Item` into pytest, which is formally located in the test directory.
See `generated_tests.py`.

fix http parser: avoid out-of-bounds read in upgrade detection

1. IsWebSocketUpgradeRequest scans the whole peeked socket buffer for "Upgrade:" and then skips trailing spaces with `while (*it == ' ' && it != req.end())`, dereferencing the iterator before testing it against the end.
2. When the buffer ends with "Upgrade:" followed by spaces that run to the exact end, the loop walks to req.end() and reads one byte past the buffer; the next line then forms `it + kWebsocketUpgradeHeaderValue.size()`, a pointer past one-past-the-end. This is reachable before auth: a CONNECT request carries no Upgrade header, so llhttp returns HPE_PAUSED_UPGRADE and Parse() runs this probe over a buffer whose only "Upgrade:" is attacker-appended trailing bytes.

Reordered the loop to check the end iterator first and replaced the pointer walk with a remaining-length comparison, which keeps the existing accept/reject behavior. Verified under AddressSanitizer by feeding the bundled llhttp a CONNECT request ending in "Upgrade:" plus spaces (heap-buffer-overflow read of size 1 before the patch, clean after).

feat userver: add sql DTO generation

### Changelog entry

* PostgreSQL
  * Added DTO codegen to `userver_add_sql_library`: passing the `DTO_DIALECT postgresql`
    argument now generates a typed C++ client from your migrations and queries.
    You get `struct`s / `enum class`es, an
    abstract `PgClient` interface, a `ClusterPgClient` running over a @ref storages::postgres::Cluster,
    and a gmock-based `MockPgClient` for unit tests. See @ref sql_dto.
  * Added the `userver::postgresql-utest` testing library for writing `UTEST`-based PostgreSQL tests
    against a real database.
  * Added the `samples/postgres_dto_service` example service demonstrating the generated client end to end.

### Description

The generator dumps the database schema into a JSON file (`schema.dto.json`) and emits C++ files from it.

The flow is:

* **Schema.** Collect all migrations, apply them, and read the user-defined
  types and tables back from the system catalogs. From that it generates the DTOs (`struct`s /
  `enum class`es) plus an auxiliary migration that declares helper PG composite types (a row type per
  table).
* **Queries.** Analyze each `.sql` query — the core mechanism is a `PREPARE` statement plus a pg cursor
  to read the metadata of the result columns and the parameters.

Inferring types perfectly and unambiguously is hard, so per-query annotations (`@arg<N>`,
`@cardinality`, `@no-dto`) let you customize the analysis and the generated signatures.

The schema JSON is keyed by a hash of the migrations and queries and committed to the repo, so normal
builds and CI read it instead of starting a database; when it is stale the build fails and prints the
command to refresh it.

**Current state and limitations.**

* PostgreSQL is the only supported dialect.
* This is a deliberately conservative first version: queries default to `many` cardinality (returning
  `std::vector<...>`), and composite-type fields are always `std::optional<>`. Tighter inference is
  left for later.
* Integration is via the CMake build (`userver_add_sql_library`).

**Further plans.**

* More dialects beyond PostgreSQL.
* Support transaction and other userver feature in the typed client.
* Smarter cardinality / nullability inference so fewer queries need annotations.
* `ya.make` / codegen35 plugin.
* Allow user's cpp types and aliases.

feat chaotic: make additionalProperties logic compatible with jsonschema spec

**Changelog entry:**

chaotic:

* Aligned `additionalProperties` handling with the JSON Schema specification.

  Previously, omitting `additionalProperties` from an object schema was treated the same as `additionalProperties: false`, which caused generated structs to reject unknown JSON fields. According to the JSON Schema spec, an absent `additionalProperties` key means unknown fields are permitted.

  New behavior:
  - Absent `additionalProperties` (key not present in YAML/JSON): unknown fields are silently ignored (non-strict parsing). No `extra` member is generated.
  - `additionalProperties: true`: an `extra` member of type `formats::json::Value` is generated, and known fields use strict parsing. To suppress the `extra` member while preserving "ignore unknowns" semantics, use `x-usrv-extra-member: false`.
  - `additionalProperties: false` or a typed schema: behavior unchanged.

* Renamed extension properties `x-usrv-cpp-extra-member` and `x-taxi-cpp-extra-member` to `x-usrv-extra-member` and `x-taxi-extra-member` respectively. The old names are no longer recognized.

* Added support for `x-usrv-strict-parsing` as an alias for `x-taxi-strict-parsing`. This attribute allows to fail parsing on extra fields for an object even if extra fields are allowed globally.

* `CompilerBase.__init__` now requires `strict_parsing_default` as a mandatory keyword-only argument. All dynamic-config compiler callers pass `strict_parsing_default=False` to preserve backward compatibility.

feat userver/testsuite: add controls for cache sync updates

In testsuite, a `POST /tests/control` request with full cache invalidation used to update `dynamic-config-client-updater` synchronously first, while a custom dynamic config updater ran in the shared concurrent pool. As a result, config-dependent caches could refresh before new dynamic config values were applied — especially on services that migrate from the built-in updater to a custom one.

Now, updaters listed in `cache-reverse-dependencies` are refreshed synchronously before the parallel reset of the remaining caches.

## **Details**

* Extended testsuite cache reset ordering: reverse dependencies are no longer hardcoded to a single built-in updater name.

* Added `cache-reverse-dependencies` to `testsuite-support` static config (default includes the built-in dynamic config updater).

fix install: auto-derive components, multipackage .deb fix, sample install

### What

Refactors the userver install & CPack packaging layer and fixes several install regressions.

### Why

The install rules had grown brittle: the list of findable `find_package(userver COMPONENTS ...)` components was maintained by hand and drifted from reality, the multipackage `.deb` build silently skipped `libuserver-core-dev`, and the `easy` library samples were never shipped (so they weren't exercised by the "build every installed sample" CI check).

### Changes

- Auto-derive `USERVER_AVAILABLE_COMPONENTS`. A component becomes findable exactly when it installs real library targets, collected through a global property. Removed the 17 hand-maintained `list(APPEND USERVER_AVAILABLE_COMPONENTS ...)` entries. Added a `NON_FINDABLE` opt-out to `_userver_install_targets`.
- Multipackage `.deb` install fix. Corrected the install glob in `scripts/build_and_install.sh` so `libuserver-core-dev` (binary + samples) is actually installed.
- Folded the "dangling" `postgres`/`sqldto` install components into `postgresql` component for now.
- API cleanup. Renamed `_userver_install_component(MODULE ...)` → `COMPONENT`; and `userver_module(DEPENDS ...)` → `COMPONENT_DEPENDS`; `_userver_directory_install` gains `EXCLUDE_PATTERNS` (multi-value).
- Ship the `easy` library samples as a standalone project under `share/userver/samples/easy`; the subdirectory-build-only stub stays in `libraries/easy/CMakeLists.txt`.
- Fixed installation of non-main modules like `libraries/protobuf` and `grpc/handlers`, which belong to a component, but aren't responsible for its creation.
- CI hardening. The "build every installed sample" loop now fails fast if no samples were installed.

### Changelog entry

* Fixed `libuserver-core-dev` not being installed when building the multipackage Debian packages (`USERVER_INSTALL_MULTIPACKAGE=1`).
* The set of components usable with `find_package(userver COMPONENTS ...)` is now derived automatically from the install rules, so newly added components are findable without extra bookkeeping.
* The `easy` library samples are now installed under `share/userver/samples/easy` and built as a standalone project.

fix postgres: bound-check buffer in inet/cidr/macaddr parsers

Repro: a Postgres server returns an inet/cidr field shorter than its 4-byte header (or a 4-byte header that declares a 16-byte address with no address bytes present), or a macaddr field shorter than its 6/8 octets.
Cause: the inet/cidr parser in ip.hpp and the macaddr parser in macaddr.hpp read the fixed header and then memcpy the address bytes straight from FieldBuffer::buffer without checking FieldBuffer::length, so a short field reads past the end of the buffer (ASan reports a 16-byte heap read one byte past a 4-byte region).
Fix: validate buffer.length against the header size and the declared address length before reading, throwing InvalidInputBufferSize the same way the rest of the io layer does for short buffers. Added a unit test covering the short inet/cidr/macaddr cases.

feat core: tp logger consumer wakeup notification batching

Changelog entry:

* Improved async logging performance under load: the writer task is no longer woken on every log line. Notifications between periodic flushes are batched while the message queue is less than half full (the periodic flush drains it), which cuts most of the `futex_wake` syscalls. For example, on our userver grpc load-testing service, with server logs enabled, `fs-task-processor` CPU usage dropped from ~5% to ~0.5%.

---

**Idea.** For performance, we try to batch the consumer notifications that happen between flushes: as long as the queue size allows (it is not yet half full), a plain log does not wake the consumer, and the wakeup is left to the periodic `log_flusher`. This cuts most of the `futex_wake` calls that previously happened on almost every log line.

**How.** `TpLogger` gets a configurable batching mode (`SetNotificationBatching`): a log wakes the consumer only if it is flush-worthy (level ≥ flush level) or the queue is at least half full; otherwise the notification is batched and deferred to the periodic flush. In `AsyncFlatCombiningQueue` the push takes a `NotificationMode {kNotify, kDeferred}`, and the sleeping/awake state is tracked by a small atomic state machine instead of a sentinel node, so wakeups stay race-free with no lost notifications.

Synchronous logging is unchanged; testsuite log capture temporarily disables batching for immediate delivery.

No changelog entry intended, no effects on API or measurable effects on performance.

* `engine::impl::Awaiter` is now passed around in `AwaiterPtr`, which is a `unique_ptr` with a custom deleter that decrements the intrusive refcounter of `TaskContext` calls virtual `PolymorphicAwaiter::DisposeWithoutNotification` on destruction.

      * `unique_ptr` better suits `AwaitableBase` API, which are the majority of awaitables. Only legacy `WaitAny` actually copies the `intrusive_ptr`.
      * `unique_ptr` better suits most awaiters, which don't support being notified concurrently. And those that do can easily add an explicit `AsAwaiterPtr` method, see e.g. `WaitAnyContext::Impl`.
         * Making an expensive locked increment an explicit operation can be seen as an additional benefit.
      * The existing performance of `TaskContext` awaiter is maintained, there are still no virtual calls for this kind of `Awaiter`.

* Added `IntrusiveRefCounterOne` as a common place for intrusive refcounter that initializes to 1 instead of 0 (that place was `Awaiter` previously).

Breaking changes:

* Monotonic counter metrics in `postgresql`, `mysql`, `clickhouse`, `kafka`, `rabbitmq`, `redis`, core `dist_lock`, `congestion_control` and the `websocket` handler are now reported as `RATE` instead of `GAUGE` (see @ref scripts/docs/en/userver/metrics.md); a few metrics keep their legacy `GAUGE` value and additionally report a new `.v2` `RATE` metric until dashboards/alerts are migrated.

- `ws.<handler_name>.msg.sent`, `ws.<handler_name>.msg.recv`, `ws.<handler_name>.bytes.sent`, `ws.<handler_name>.bytes.recv`

- `clickhouse.connections.created`, `clickhouse.connections.closed`, `clickhouse.connections.overload`, `clickhouse.queries.total`, `clickhouse.queries.error`, `clickhouse.inserts.total`, `clickhouse.inserts.error`

- `rabbitmq.<component_name>.<host>.connections_created`, `rabbitmq.<component_name>.<host>.connections_closed`, `rabbitmq.<component_name>.<host>.bytes_sent`, `rabbitmq.<component_name>.<host>.bytes_read`, `rabbitmq.<component_name>.<host>.messages_published`, `rabbitmq.<component_name>.<host>.messages_consumed`
- `redis-pubsub.messages.count`, `redis-pubsub.messages.alien-count`, `redis-pubsub.messages.size`
- `postgresql.connections.opened`, `postgresql.connections.closed`, `postgresql.connections.rate-limit-throttled`, `postgresql.transactions.total`, `postgresql.transactions.no-tran`, `postgresql.queries.parsed`, `postgresql.queries.portals-bound`, `postgresql.queries.replies`

feat userver/protobuf:  add `protobuf::json::MessageToJsonString`

* Added @ref protobuf::json::MessageToJsonString, which is up to 5 times faster than `google::protobuf::util::MessageToJsonString` on synthetic benchmarks.

feat userver: add aimd limiter

The utils::AimdLimiter has been added — an adaptive limiter that dynamically adjusts its limit based on feedback on the success of operations.

The limiter uses the AIMD (Additive Increase Multiplicative Decrease) algorithm — a classic approach to congestion management that ensures system stability and quick response to problems:

- During successful operations (OnSuccess()), the limit is smoothly increased additively (by addition): the increase occurs slowly and carefully.
- During unsuccessful operations (OnFailure()), the limit is sharply reduced multiplicatively (by multiplication): the decrease occurs quickly and aggressively.

Slow growth allows the system to carefully explore the available bandwidth.
Quick reduction provides an immediate response to congestion and protects the system from cascading failures.
This behavior makes the system stable and resistant to load fluctuations.

fix kafka: fix install script, add tests and fixes on task cancellation during kafka producer Send

Fixes a Use-After-Free vulnerability in the asynchronous Kafka Producer API when a task is cancelled before librdkafka flushes its queue.

The kafka::Producer::Send API accepts parameters as views (string_view, zstring_view, HeaderViews). These views point to data owned by the caller. Inside Send, raw pointers from these views are passed down to librdkafka, which stores them in its internal asynchronous queues for background delivery.

If a client connection drops, a cascade cancellation of tasks occurs. This leads to a premature return from kafka::Producer::Send, causing the caller to destroy the original payload memory. However, librdkafka still retains these pointers and attempts to access them during subsequent network flushes to the broker, resulting in memory corruption.

To fix this:
* ensure that `WaitUntilAllMessagesDelivered` is executed even if the task is cancelled and the exceptions from it are logged;
* ensure that `WaitUntilDeliveryReported` is not interrupted by cancel.

fix redis: use FromString for double reply values

1. `Parse(..., To<double>)` converts floating-point reply values (`ZSCORE`, `HINCRBYFLOAT`, `ZADD ... INCR`) with `std::stod`, which respects the process `LC_NUMERIC` and keeps only the valid numeric prefix of the string.

Added a regression test for the trailing-junk case along with valid and infinite values.

fix redis: check geo reply member is a string before GetString

ParseReplyDataArray for GeoPoint in redis/src/storages/redis/parse_reply.cpp reads the first element of each per-member sub-array of a GEORADIUS/GEOSEARCH reply with GetString(), but only checks that the sub-array is non-empty rather than that the element is a string. fix websocket: apply control frame length limit to ping and pong

1. `is_data_frame` in `ReadWSFrameImpl` classifies the opcode with `opcode & (kText | kBinary)`, so ping (0x9) and pong (0xA) both test non-zero and count as data frames. The RFC 6455 5.5 guard just below it, which rejects a control frame with `payload_len > 125`, never fires for them, and a client can send a ping carrying up to `max-remote-payload` bytes.
2. That payload is echoed back in a pong. `MakeControlFrame` assigns the size into a 7-bit field while `SendFrame` writes the payload in full, so a 200-byte ping is answered with `8A 48` followed by 200 bytes. The peer takes 72 of them as the pong and parses the remaining 128 as further frames.
3. Compared the opcode against the three data opcodes instead of masking, which puts ping and pong back under the existing control frame check.
4. Control frames may legally arrive inside a fragmented message, so the pong now echoes only the ping's own bytes rather than the whole accumulated buffer, which can still hold an unfinished data frame.

Added `protocol_test.cpp` covering the oversized ping and pong, a 125-byte ping, and a ping interleaved with a fragmented text message. The three new negative cases fail on the current tree (kNone instead of kProtocolError) and pass with the change; the rest of `userver-core-unittest` is unaffected.

fix universal: validate address size in CidrNetworkFromInetNetwork

1. CidrNetworkFromInetNetwork copies the InetNetwork byte vector into a fixed-size std::array (4 bytes for NetworkV4, 16 for NetworkV6) with std::ranges::copy and never checks that the source length matches the destination.
2. InetNetwork holds the parsed bytes of a PostgreSQL inet/cidr value, whose 4- or 16-byte length follows the server-supplied family. Converting a 16-byte IPv6 value through NetworkV4FromInetNetwork copies 16 bytes into the 4-byte array (a 12-byte out-of-bounds stack write); the reverse case leaves 12 destination bytes uninitialized.
3. Require inet_bytes.size() == bytes.size() and throw std::invalid_argument on mismatch, mirroring the size and family validation already performed in the InetNetwork constructor.

Verified with a regression in ip_test.cpp: the IPv6-to-NetworkV4 case trips AddressSanitizer (stack-buffer-overflow, 16-byte write into a 4-byte array) on the current tree and throws std::invalid_argument after the change. The valid same-family conversions are unaffected.

feat odbc: make driver production-ready

Fixes https://github.com/userver-framework/userver/issues/218

This is a follow-up to #1161 that completes the remaining ODBC production-readiness work and addresses the maintainer feedback from that review.

## What changed

- Added secure parameterized query execution for `Cluster` and `Transaction` using ODBC `?` placeholders, `SQLPrepare`, `SQLNumParams`, `SQLBindParameter`, and `SQLExecute`. The public API supports booleans, integer and floating-point types, strings, enums, optionals, and null values while keeping bound storage alive for the entire execution.
- Exposed `CommandControl` as public API, merged explicit/default/inherited deadlines, removed public `engine::Deadline` overloads, and made network deadlines cover connection acquisition, connect, begin, and blocking statement execution.
- Added post-call deadline checks so a driver call that completes after its deadline is reported as `OperationInterrupted` and accounted as a timeout.
- Added live secdist updates without replacing the public `Cluster`, with serialized topology replacement, unchanged-DSN suppression, safe pool/connection lifetime, and restoration of per-pool static settings when a dynamic override disappears.
- Added component and dynamic-config schema documentation, snippet-backed user documentation, configuration validation, an ODBC metrics smoke test, and a secdist reload functional test.
- Incorporated the smaller review fixes from #1161 (`StrIcaseEqual`, `utils::text::ToUpper`, designated initializers, and safe atomic ordering).

## User impact

ODBC users can pass query parameters separately from SQL text instead of formatting them into a query, configure operation timeouts through the same command-control model as other userver database drivers, reload DSNs through secdist, and rely on documented schemas and metrics.

## Validation

- ODBC PostgreSQL test suite: 69/69 passed
- ODBC basic-chaos functional suite: 15/15 passed
- ODBC secdist-update functional suite: 1/1 passed
- `userver-odbc` and both functional services built successfully
- component-schema and dynamic-config documentation generators passed
- project `clang-format --dry-run --Werror`, `git diff --check`, JSON validation, and Python syntax checks passed

feat redis: release command callbacks on timeout

## Problem

When a Redis command timed out, it was logically completed with `kTimeoutError` and marked `invoke_disabled`, but `SingleCommand::meta` retained the `Command` until a late hiredis reply or disconnect. For Sentinel requests, this kept `GetHostsContext` and its shared `ScopeGuard` alive, leaving `update_topology_flag_` set. Subsequent topology updates were skipped, so failover and master/replica changes could remain unnoticed until a disconnect or component recreation.

## Changes

- Move `command.meta` out of `SingleCommand` before invoking the timeout callback. `SingleCommand` remains alive for hiredis bookkeeping and safe late-reply handling, while callback captures are released immediately after logical completion.
- Remove the temporary workaround that recreated `Sentinel` and `SubscribeSentinel` for every retry.
- Add a deterministic regression test with a delayed mock Redis reply. It verifies that the callback is released before the late reply, is not invoked twice, and that the next command succeeds.

feat crypto: support IPAddress SAN for TLS, add diagnostics for ClickHouse

We previously started passing ClickHouse host as TLS `server_name`, so `SSL_VERIFY_PEER` is on. OpenSSL hostname checks (`X509_VERIFY_PARAM_set1_host`) match only dNSName/CN, not iPAddress SANs. A certificate issued for an IP then fails the handshake.

This change keeps the added verify path and makes IP hosts use the matching OpenSSL API:

- empty `server_name`: no peer verify (unchanged)
- non-empty `server_name`: `SSL_VERIFY_PEER` stays on
- hostname: `X509_VERIFY_PARAM_set1_host`
- IP: `X509_VERIFY_PARAM_set1_ip_asc` (iPAddress SAN)
- SNI (`SSL_set_tlsext_host_name`) is still skipped for IPs (RFC 6066)
- ClickHouse logs the real connect exception instead of swallowing it

Tests cover a trusted IP-SAN cert, a mismatched IP, and a mismatched hostname.

fix redis: start Redis command watcher before publishing kConnected

## Problem

Sentinel can observe `kConnected` and enqueue `SENTINEL MASTERS` before `watch_command_` is started. `ev_async_start` resets `w->sent`, the wakeup is lost, and the command stays in the queue forever — topology never arrives, the service fails to start.

## Fix

Start the command watcher (and ping/info timers) **before** publishing `kConnected`, so `AsyncCommand` cannot lose its wakeup.

## Tests

`Redis::CommandImmediatelyAfterConnected` waits for `kConnected` via `signal_state_change`, then sends `GET` from the test coroutine and expects a reply (no busy-loop).

bug mongo: initialize mongoc_init before main

`mongoc_init` uses `pthread_once` and calls `getenv`. Doing that on a userver coroutine stack (including the blocking task processor) crashes under ASan: `getenv` is not safe with `makecontext`/`swapcontext`.

Initialize via a process-lifetime `GlobalInitializer` in `wrappers.cpp` so `mongoc_init` runs before `main`, while other threads do not exist yet. Drop the lazy init from the pool constructor. `CDriverPoolImpl` odr-uses `kInitMongoc` so the initializer stays linked when the pool is used.

If mongo is linked into a service binary but is not actually used, the linker may drop it. If it is kept, that is fine: `mongoc_init` does not create threads, does not open network connections, and does not cause ongoing CPU use or significant memory use.

## Load testing

We loaded 8 cpu (==8 workers) with 15k RPS. Latency in the new scheduler got 15-20% smaller than in the old scheduler.

`TaskProcessor::ProcessTasks` is 3% smaller on flamegraphs in the new scheduler.

# Architecture

1. Local queue is the same in both schedulers.
2. Stealing and sleeping is the same.
3. The new scheduler has no local queues for background work. Background work is passed to the global queue instead.
4. There a global intrusive queue locked by `std::mutex` in the new scheduler instead of moodycamel in the old scheduler. (This is something worth exploring in the future.)

fix websocket: correct frame length encoding for 32768–65535-byte payloads

DataFrameHeader selected the 64-bit length encoding for payloads larger than INT16_MAX. For payloads of 32768–65535 bytes, this violates the minimal length encoding requirement in RFC 6455 Section 5.2, causing Chromium to reject these frames with Invalid frame header. For example, a 38874-byte message used length marker 127 instead of 126.

This change replaces the threshold with UINT16_MAX and encodes lengths using uint16_t and uint64_t. The regression test compares the exact header bytes for payload lengths of 0, 125, 126, 32767, 32768, 38874, 65535, and 65536 bytes, with the masking flag both set and unset.

RFC: <https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6455#section-5.2>

bug redis: do not throw when unsubscribing in a cancelled task

Problem. Releasing a subscription sends UNSUBSCRIBE through
Sentinel::AsyncCommand(), which rejects commands from a cancelled task and
drops them on an expired inherited deadline. Tokens are released in
destructors, so RequestCancelledException escaped a noexcept context and
aborted candidates-virt when component load was cancelled during a geobus
subscribe.

Change. impl::SubscriptionToken::Unsubscribe() is noexcept: it drops the
subscription id upfront, calls the storage under
engine::TaskCancellationBlocker and
server::request::DeadlinePropagationBlocker, and logs the rest, following
dist_lock::LockGuard::TryUnlock().

Effects. Failures are no longer reported to the caller; the callback is
erased before any command is sent, so nothing calls back after
Unsubscribe() returns.
